cultural.vision_reason: A woven silk-and-cotton hair-band made at Egga on the Niger, worn by women of the higher classes as a hair ornament—this is plausible Nupe-area material culture (Egga was a Nupe/Nupe-adjacent riverine town), worn as an item of adornment.

physical.title: hair-band
physical.summary:
(description from 1843-5 Register)
Female hair band weaved with raw silk, excepting that of the blue stripe, made of of cotton. It is used by the higher classes; the hair being platted in the shape of a half moon, with a country cloth (not the best quality) over the head leaving the face uncovered when walking about, and only exposed on a visit or paying compliments to respectable people. Made at Egga on the banks of the Niger. One breadth, 1 3/4 ins wide, length 8ft 11 ins. Paid 2000 cowries. It is a rude crimson ribband with two blue and yellow stripes.

(modern description)
A single very narrow, but very long, strip of cloth to be used as a head-tie: it is hand-woven using predominantly hand-spun magenta alaari silk in both warp and weft, with the exception of two narrow stripes, consisting of four rows of white alternating with four rows of indigo cotton, which replace the alaari in the warp; these are placed towards the sides of the strip.
